_note: Per-position and per-trade rationale. Loaded by ibkr_dashboard and merged into transactions.csv export.

SNAP.explanation: First live IBKR trade ever, sized intentionally tiny ($5.21) as a system reliability test rather than for return. Original $10-budget plan was to buy 1 share of F, but during the session the user explicitly capped exposure for the night and SNAP was the only screened candidate ≤ $10 single share ($5.71 → filled at $5.21 in 4 AM pre-market). Selected via momentum screener: passed 30-day positive momentum (+7%) and >$50M daily $ volume; not a high-conviction pick but the cheapest passable name. Filled at pre-market open exactly when the limit was reached.
SNAP.protective_stops: NONE attached (day-1 of holding; IBKR day-trade rule restricts same-day sell). OCA bracket will auto-attach on day-2 by watcher daemon.
SNAP.exit_plan: Watcher will compute adaptive trail = BASE_K × ATR × VIX_mult × SPY_trend × burst_mult, clipped [2%, 8%]. Hard stop = entry × (1 − min(10%, 2×ATR)). OCA group binds the two server-side at IBKR so either fill cancels the other. Time-stop at 7 days idle.

F.explanation: Arm A of the three-arm $60 experiment. F (Ford) selected as the balanced-philosophy representative: moderate ATR (4.9%), steady 30d momentum (+8%), strong 90d (+25%). Sized to 1 share (~$14.41) — single-share is the only option without IBKR fractional permission (account-locked for 28 days). The 'balanced' regime ($A) treats profit/risk equally: BASE_K=2.25 trail, 10% hard stop. Goal: provide a baseline against which arms B (aggressive) and C (QC-substitute) can be measured.
F.protective_stops: NONE attached (day-1, same as SNAP). Day-2 watcher will attach OCA bracket.
F.exit_plan: Adaptive trail ~8% (capped), hard stop 10%, profit-step at +2×ATR (sell half, ratchet trail to BE — requires qty≥2, won't trigger on 1-share), time stop 7d idle.

AAL.explanation: Arm B of the three-arm $60 experiment — the 'higher risk, higher return' philosophy (75% profit-seeking / 25% risk-mitigation tilt). AAL chosen as the strongest momentum pick from the screener: +28% 30d, +52% 90d, ATR 4.2%. Travel/airline sector rotation tailwind. Sized 1 share (~$15.79). The aggressive regime gets a wider trail (let winners run) and no profit-step (don't take chips off the table early). Tradeoff: more giveback in drawdowns but more capture in trending moves.
AAL.exit_plan: Wider adaptive trail: BASE_K × 1.25 (scaled looser for arm B), hard stop 12% (vs 10% balanced), no profit-step. Time stop 7d idle.

PINS.explanation: Arm C of the three-arm experiment — substitute for the QC top-5 momentum rotation. Original intent was to use the same picks as the Alpaca QC bot (AMD, NVDA, AAPL, GOOGL, JPM), but those all trade $170-$540/share — impossible to buy 1 share within a $20-per-arm budget on IBKR (no fractional permission). PINS chosen as a close substitute: also a momentum-driven cheap name (rank #4 in the screener at +12% 30d, +18% 90d), social/ad sector for diversification within the experiment. The QC-style profile gets the disciplined adaptive trail (default BASE_K=2.25), tightest hard stop in the experiment (8%), and active profit-step.
PINS.exit_plan: Adaptive trail BASE_K=2.25, hard stop 8% (tightest of the three arms), profit-step at +2×ATR active, time stop 7d idle.
